step-1.text: Stand one side panel on its edge, holes facing in. Screw in ten cam pins by hand, then tap in ten dowels.

count-1.text: This step uses 1 side panel, 10 cam pins and 10 wood dowels.

step-2.text: Push the bottom panel onto the low pins and dowels. Drop two cam locks into the round holes, arrows facing the pins, and turn them clockwise until they grab.

count-2.text: This step uses 1 bottom panel and 2 cam locks.

step-3.text: The fixed shelves hold the bookcase square, so they go in now. Slide onto the pins and lock with cam locks, clockwise.

count-3.text: This step uses 4 fixed shelves and 8 cam locks.

step-4.text: Tap dowels into the panel below, then press the divider down onto them. Dowels go in the top end too, ready for what sits above.

count-4.text: This step uses 1 divider and 4 wood dowels.

step-5.text: Pins and dowels go into the ends of the panels on this side too. With a helper, lower the second side onto all of them at once, then lock the last ten cam locks.

count-5.text: This step uses 1 side panel, 10 cam pins, 10 wood dowels and 10 cam locks.

step-6.text: Tap four dowels into the top edges of the sides. Set the top panel on, good side up, then lock it from inside with four cam locks.

count-6.text: This step uses 1 top panel, 4 wood dowels and 4 cam locks.

step-7.text: Tap four dowels into the ends of the plinth board and press it in under the bottom panel, at the front.

count-7.text: This step uses 1 plinth and 4 wood dowels.

step-8.text: Roll the bookcase over so it lies on its front. Ask your helper, and put the flattened box underneath to save the finish.

count-8.text: Nothing new this step. Just you and the frame.

step-9.text: Lay the back panel on, smooth side facing in. Line it up with the bottom corners and nail it along the edges, about every twenty centimeters. If the corners line up, the bookcase is square.

step-10.text: Second back piece, butted tight against the first. Same nailing pattern along every edge.

step-11.text: Stand it up together. Lift with your legs, not your back.

count-11.text: Nothing new this step. Just you and the frame.

step-12.text: Screw the metal runners inside the frame, one pair for each drawer, four in all. Use the pre-drilled holes so every pair sits level.

count-12.text: This step uses 4 drawer runners and 8 screws.

step-13.text: First drawer. Lay the drawer front face down on something soft. Tap in four dowels, then press both drawer sides onto them, grooves facing in.

count-13.text: This step uses 1 drawer front, 2 drawer sides and 4 wood dowels.

step-14.text: Slide the thin drawer bottom into the grooves, shiny side up, all the way to the front.

step-15.text: Close the drawer with its back panel, then drive four screws through the back into the sides. Snug, not cranked.

count-15.text: This step uses 1 drawer back and 4 screws.

step-16.text: Now the second drawer, exactly the same way: front, sides, bottom, back. Then slide every drawer in onto its runners until it stops. The demo leaves drawer one pulled open so you can see inside. Take a break halfway if you need one.

count-16.text: This step uses 1 drawer front, 2 drawer sides, 1 drawer bottom, 1 drawer back, 4 wood dowels and 4 screws.

step-17.text: Last step, and the most important. Screw the wall bracket to the top at the back, then fix it to the wall with screws that suit your wall. Furniture can tip over. Always anchor it.

done.text: Done. Your HOLMES wide bookcase with drawers is built. Give it a proud little pat.
